result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right, and both recommend simplified favicon and stitch versions plus a sew-out sample. B wins narrowly: it places the blame more clearly on the unadapted artwork, explains how gaps and letter counters fill in, and keeps the work small by building one simplified mark that is reused. A covers gradients and low-contrast colors better and gives a handy one-line brief for the designer, but its fixes are spread across more separate steps. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the designer is partly right, recommend simplified favicon and stitch versions, and suggest a sew-out before the full order. B is more complete on causes: it names gradients, low-contrast color pairs, thread layering and fabric stretch, and ties them to both the tab icon and the polos. It also ends with a usable one-sentence brief. A covers the basics well, but it barely touches on color and contrast, and its closing note about not having the logo files in the directory is out of place.
